text: Iudex Gundyr serves as a sentry who tests Unkindled travelers at the end of the Cemetery of Ash.
The Ashen One defeats Iudex Gundyr after pulling the coiled sword from his body, which releases him from his dormant state.
Vordt of the Boreal Valley guards the gate beneath the High Wall of Lothric, having become a beast-like creature due to the curse.
The Cursed Greatwood is a massive tree in the Undead Settlement that has absorbed the curses of countless undead, worshipped by villagers as a way to remove their afflictions.
The Ashen One defeats the Cursed Greatwood by destroying its cursed core after falling into a hidden altar pit beneath the village plaza.
The inner sanctum of the Cathedral of the Deep is guarded by the Deacons of the Deep, a congregation led by Archdeacon Royce.
During the fight with the Deacons of the Deep, a red glow representing a possessing evil soul jumps between deacon bodies, and only destroying the possessed body permanently ends the threat.
When the possessing evil soul animating the Deacons of the Deep is destroyed, the rest of the congregation collapses lifelessly.
The Ashen One fights through the chaotic civil war of the Abyss Watchers in the great hall of Farron Keep.
After the last Abyss Watcher falls, the order's shared soul coalesces into him, and he rises again empowered with the cinder's fire as a second phase of the boss fight.
Highlord Wolnir's golden bracelets hold back the Abyss's corruption and are his only vulnerability in battle.
When all of Highlord Wolnir's bracelets are destroyed, the Abyss fully claims him and drags him down into darkness, ending his existence.
Pontiff Sulyvahn fights the Ashen One with twin greatswords and can summon a phantom shadow clone of himself mid-battle that mirrors his movements.
The Ashen One defeats Pontiff Sulyvahn, ending his tyrannical rule over Irithyll of the Boreal Valley.
By the time the Ashen One reaches Anor Londo, Aldrich's lower body has dissolved into a slug-like sludge mass and he wields Gwyndolin's still-animate, partially eaten torso as a weapon and puppet.
In the fight against Aldrich, he uses stolen abilities from Gwyndolin including soul spears and twisted miracles, plus a manifested lifehunt scythe inspired by dream-visions of a hidden pale girl.
Defeating Aldrich causes him to dissolve, leaving behind a cleric's staff and the Cinders of a Lord, confirming his status as a Lord of Cinder.
After Aldrich's death, his monstrous form dissolved, revealing Gwyndolin's remains had finally stopped moving inside him.
Yhorm the Giant retreated to his throne room, sitting with his great machete across his knees, waiting without purpose.
When the Ashen One confronted Yhorm the Giant, a Storm Ruler greatsword lay near his throne, possibly placed deliberately by Yhorm himself.
In some versions of the fight, Siegward of Catarina arrives to help the Ashen One defeat Yhorm the Giant, honoring his old promise.
The Ashen One defeated Yhorm the Giant and claimed his cinders of a lord, marking the third Lord of Cinder dealt with.
The Dancer of the Boreal Valley, one of Pontiff Sulyvahn's Outrider Knights, appeared in the chapel after Emma's death to stop the Ashen One.
The Dancer of the Boreal Valley wields one sword burning with phantom flame and another emanating cold dark mist.
The Ashen One defeated the Dancer of the Boreal Valley, who collapsed into black ash.
The Dragon Slayer Armor, an ancient relic from the age of dragon-hunting knights, is animated by pilgrim butterflies and guards the bridge to the Grand Archives.
The Dragon Slayer Armor wields a massive great axe and shield, both crackling with lightning.
The Ashen One defeated the Dragon Slayer Armor, causing it to collapse and the controlling pilgrim butterflies to scatter.
A surviving Crystal Sage, the sibling of the one fought in the Cathedral of the Deep's woods, appears in the Grand Archives allied with Lothric.
The Ashen One defeated the surviving Crystal Sage in the Grand Archives.
At the top of the Grand Archives, three elite warriors called the Three Pillars of the king's rule - Lion Knight Albert, Black Hand Kamui, and Cream Hild - guard the path to Prince Lothric.
Lion Knight Albert fights with disciplined, precise sword and shield technique in service to the king.
Black Hand Kamui is a royal assassin who fights with twin blades and extreme speed.
Cream Hild is a sorceress who provides magical support with crystal projectiles and energy bolts.
The Ashen One defeated the Three Pillars (Albert, Kamui, and Cream Hild) one at a time on a balcony above the Grand Archives.
Prince Lothric sits on a throne, pale, sickly, and physically weak, but possesses arcane abilities.
Lorian is Prince Lothric's elder brother, once a renowned knight, who knelt before the throne, having lost the use of his legs and voice.
Lorian cannot walk and instead teleports in bursts of flame, fighting with a blazing greatsword.
Lorian, the crippled elder prince, fights the Ashen One in the Lothric Castle throne room to protect his brother Lothric.

After Lorian collapses, Lothric climbs onto his brother's back and the two fight together as a combined being; alternatively, Lothric supports Lorian with healing and augmenting spells and revives him when he falls.
While bonded together, Lothric casts miracles and homing soul projectiles while Lorian presses the physical assault with his flaming sword.
Lorian and Lothric are ultimately both defeated and die together, their bound souls reaching their end simultaneously.
The Soul of Cinder is an entity formed from the merged souls of every Lord of Cinder who has ever linked the flame, acting as the final guardian of the first flame.
The Soul of Cinder wields the Firelink Greatsword, a coiled blade matching the Coiled Sword the Ashen One originally pulled from Iudex Gundyr.

During the fight, the Soul of Cinder shifts unpredictably between combat styles, including a knight's straight sword, a sorcerer's staff, a flaming curved blade for pyromancy, and a polearm paired with miracles.
In its final phase, the Soul of Cinder's coiled sword bursts into golden flame and its moveset shifts to channel the fighting style of Lord Gwyn himself.
Gwyn's channeled moveset within the Soul of Cinder includes leaping attacks covering great distances, crackling lightning bolts, and a plunging thrust originally used to slay dragons.
The Ashen One defeats the Soul of Cinder, causing the amalgamated armor of past champions to crumble into ash.
Sir Vilhelm is a knight loyal to Sister Frieda who guards the deeper reaches of the Painted World of Ariandel.

The Ashen One fights Father Ariandel and Sister Frieda across a multi-phase battle, with Ariandel reigniting the suppressed flame to revive Frieda after her first defeat; in her final phase she transforms into Black Flame Frieda, becoming faster and more aggressive, having been revived twice before being finally defeated.
At the bottom of the Dreg Heap waits the Demon Prince, formed when two lesser demons merge into one being after being defeated.
The Demon Prince is the last of the demons born from the chaos flame that originally consumed the Witch of Izalith during her failed attempt to recreate the First Flame.
The Demon Prince first appears as two demons fighting together before merging into a single more powerful being after their lesser forms are defeated.
Defeating the Demon Prince ends the legacy of the chaos flame, ensuring no more demons can spawn from that corrupted fire.
Darkeater Midir was originally tasked with protecting the Ringed City from the abyss, but was eventually corrupted by the darkness he guarded against.
In the far future wasteland, Slave Knight Gael waits among the corpses of the Pygmy Lords he has slaughtered.
By the time the Ashen One finds him in the future wasteland, Gael's body has grown huge, twisted, and skeletal, with his red cape in tatters.

A dark sign is branded onto Gael's flesh, marking him as someone who has consumed power never meant for mortal beings; consuming the Dark Soul did not strengthen him but instead broke his mind and body, as the power was too great for any being to carry.
Gael's wounds would not close and the blood of the Dark Soul continually dripped from them.
Gael greets the Ashen One by demanding their Dark Soul, beginning the final boss battle of the game, fought across the largest arena in the series.
Gael fights using sword combinations from his long life of battle experience and fires bolts from a repeating crossbow between sword strikes.
As the fight progresses, a crack opens in Gael's chest and glowing red blood infused with the Dark Soul's essence begins pouring out.
In his later phase, Gael gains dark blood magic attacks, including corrupted blood explosions from jumping slams and homing bolts of tracking blood.
The battle with Slave Knight Gael has three phases: a bestial first phase, a more human and flame-empowered second phase, and a final phase with falling red lightning.
The Ashen One defeats Slave Knight Gael using skills and lessons learned from every previous battle of the journey.
After being defeated, Gael's monstrous form fades, leaving behind simply an old knight who sacrificed everything for an unfulfilled goal.
The Abyss Watchers were an entire legion of warriors who drank from the blood of the wolf, linking their souls into one shared entity across many bodies.
The Abyss Watchers eventually became corrupted by the Abyss they hunted, turning some of them against each other in an endless internal battle.
Ringing the great bell at Archdragon Peak summons the Nameless King for a boss battle with two phases: first riding the King of the Storm, then fighting alone after absorbing his dragon's soul.
After defeating the King of the Storm, the Nameless King dismounts and absorbs his dragon companion's soul before continuing the fight alone.
The Ashen One battles Halflight, Spear of the Church, and the optional superboss Darkeater Midir, a dragon corrupted by the abyss he long consumed.
